title: WTO — World Trade Organization
shortDescription: GATT's successor: rules-based global trade, dispute settlement, and how WTO actually differs from a trade agreement.
genZNote: The referee for world trade — GATT was the practice league, WTO is the real one.

sections.heading: Full Form, Establishment, Predecessor
bullets: Established: 1 January 1995, as the successor to GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, 1948) following the Uruguay Round of negotiations (1986–1994).

Key structural difference from GATT: GATT was only a provisional multilateral agreement with a small secretariat; WTO is a full permanent organization with legal personality, its own charter (the Marrakesh Agreement), and binding dispute settlement.

sections.heading: Objectives and Core Principles
bullets: Objective: ensure trade flows as smoothly, predictably and freely as possible by administering trade agreements, providing a forum for negotiations, and settling disputes.
Most-Favoured-Nation (MFN) treatment: a trade advantage granted to one member must be granted to all WTO members equally (with specific, defined exceptions like free trade areas and customs unions).
National Treatment: imported and locally produced goods should be treated equally once the imported goods have entered the market.
Reciprocity, transparency, and special/differential treatment for developing countries are the other guiding principles.

rows: WTO's top decision-making body — all members, meets at least once every two years.
Conducts WTO's regular business between Ministerial Conferences; also convenes as the Dispute Settlement Body and the Trade Policy Review Body.
Heads the WTO Secretariat; oversees day-to-day administration, has largely managerial/advisory (not policy-making) authority since decisions are member-driven.
Handles trade disputes between members through a structured, rules-based process — widely seen as WTO's most powerful and distinctive feature versus GATT.

sections.heading: WTO and India
bullets: India is a founding member of the WTO (1995) and was also an original GATT contracting party (from 1948).
India has frequently negotiated on behalf of developing countries on issues like agricultural subsidies, food security stockholding, and special safeguard mechanisms.
India has both filed and defended WTO disputes — trade remedy and agriculture-subsidy cases are recurring themes.

sections.heading: Current Leadership (verified)
sections.body: Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria) has been WTO Director-General since March 2021 — the first woman and first African to hold the post.

sections.heading: Important Terminology
bullets: Ministerial Conference — the top WTO decision-making event, not to be confused with the annual World Economic Forum (Davos), which is unrelated.
Dumping — exporting a product at a price lower than its normal value in the home market; WTO rules allow importing countries to impose anti-dumping duties in response.
Doha Development Round — the (still incomplete) round of WTO trade negotiations launched in 2001, focused on developing-country concerns.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The WTO is the permanent, rules-based global trade organization (est. 1995, HQ Geneva) that succeeded GATT, built around MFN treatment, national treatment, and binding dispute settlement.
keyFacts: Established 1 January 1995, successor to GATT (1948), after the Uruguay Round (1986–1994).
HQ: Geneva. Top body: Ministerial Conference (meets ≥ once every 2 years).
India: founding WTO member (1995) and original GATT signatory (1948).
Current DG: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria), since March 2021 — first woman, first African DG.
commonConfusion: GATT was an agreement administered ad hoc; WTO is a full permanent organization with legal personality — they are related, not identical.

highYieldFacts: WTO established 1 Jan 1995, HQ Geneva, successor to GATT (1948).
MFN and National Treatment are WTO's two foundational non-discrimination principles.
Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala: first woman and first African WTO Director-General (since 2021).
commonTraps: Do not confuse the WTO Ministerial Conference with the UN General Assembly or with Davos/WEF — separate bodies entirely.
GATT (1948) is the predecessor AGREEMENT, not a prior name for the same organization — WTO is structurally a new, permanent organization.
mustRemember: MFN = equal trade treatment among WTO members; National Treatment = equal treatment of imported vs domestic goods once inside the market.

confusedTerms.distinction: GATT (1948) was a provisional multilateral trade agreement with a small ad hoc secretariat; WTO (1995) is a full permanent organization with legal personality and binding dispute settlement.
